description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is TransactionViewController, but this program does not view - it ADDS. Two independent sources say so: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and README.md:224 '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add |'. Both are the inverse of the prompt's mapping, and the mirror image is parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. Rule R1 governs the resolution - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and practice B4 governs the disclosure, so the divergence is documented here and never silently corrected: nothing is renamed, and no case in this folder is downgraded to read-only to match the name. PROVENANCE, PRACTICE B12: every expected value below is STATICALLY DERIVED and none was captured from a live COBOL run. It was read out of app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl paragraph by paragraph and cross-checked against four authorities - the record layout of app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy, the field widths of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY, the WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD PICTURE clauses at :47-48, and the real rows of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt. Executing the legacy program here is impossible, not merely inconvenient: the Agent Action Plan section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers, among them a COBOL compiler whose indexed file handler is disabled, the absence of any Language Environment CEE service, and the absence of a CICS emulator and of the IBM-supplied DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR copybooks. That substitution is risk R-A and is escalated in the plan rather than hidden here. WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES: READ-CXACAIX-FILE at :576-604, whose EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :588 has exactly three arms in this order - WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :589, which does nothing but CONTINUE and is traversed by case14, where CARDNINO comes back carrying 0500024453765740 because :209 copied it out of the seeded row; WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :591-596, which rejects with 'Account ID NOT found...' and is owned by case09, whose account key 00000000099 matches none of the five seeded rows; and WHEN OTHER at :597-603, which THIS case owns and which no other case in the folder reaches - case10 is the only one declaring a forced repository outcome for the read and the only one carrying a DISPLAY_LINE. Note for anyone hunting the NORMAL arm that case08 is not it: its account field is '0000000 050', which fails the IS NOT NUMERIC guard at :197 because a PIC X(11) item is NUMERIC only when all eleven characters are digits, so it is rejected at :198-202 before the read is ever issued. WHEN OTHER is written for a condition the source does not enumerate, so no arrangement of seeded rows can reach it and the arm has to be forced. THE INJECTED CONDITION, NAMED: screenRequest.forcedOutcomes declares the operation 'read' with outcome OTHER, resp 19 and resp2 0. RESP 19 is DFHRESP(NOTOPEN) - common.FileStatus.NOTOPEN - the response CICS gives for a dataset that could not be reached, and it is deliberately neither DFHRESP(NORMAL), which is 0, nor DFHRESP(NOTFND), which is 13, so it can only fall through to WHEN OTHER; RESP2 is 0, no reason code. The values are stated rather than left to a default because practice B8 wants the injected pair visible and practice B1 forbids a placeholder standing where a derived value belongs, and they are the values the run genuinely produces: the forced OTHER outcome becomes card.CardXrefRepository.ReadResult.other, which reports FileStatus.NOTOPEN as its CICS RESP and 0 as its RESP2, and the controller moves both onto WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD before the EVALUATE. Both cross-reference finders share this single 'read' key because EVALUATE TRUE at :195 chooses exactly one of them and never performs both; here it is the account-keyed finder, reached from arm one. THE DISPLAY LINE, DERIVED NOT GUESSED: :598 is DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD, and this is the only one of the three CXACAIX arms that emits a diagnostic at all. WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD are both PIC S9(09) COMP at :47-48, so each renders as exactly nine digits - the width comes from the PICTURE clause, which is practice B11 - and DISPLAY concatenates its operands at their declared widths with no separator inserted between them, so the five characters of 'RESP:' are followed immediately by nine digits, then the five of 'REAS:' and nine more. The line is therefore 5 + 9 + 5 + 9 = 28 characters and reads RESP:000000019REAS:000000000. It is recorded FIRST, ahead of the message channels, because that is the order the arm performs them in: :598 displays and only then does :599-601 compose the message it rejects with. The screen message follows on the two channels its own declarations create - WS-MESSAGE is PIC X(80) at :38 and ERRMSGO is PIC X(78) in app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY, so MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :520 loses the last two bytes on the right, and reporting only one of the two would make that loss unobservable. Three entries are therefore the two logical messages the arm produces, the diagnostic and the rejection, with the rejection reported at both of its declared widths per rule R5; where the wording of a brief and the frozen ParityCase contract disagree about how many members that is, the contract wins. THIS IS A NORMAL RETURN WITH A MESSAGE, NOT AN EXCEPTION: COTRN02C contains ZERO occurrences of CALL 'CEE3ABD' - it is an online program that sets no RETURN-CODE - so the unexpected response is surfaced to the operator as a repainted screen and nothing is thrown. expectedReturnCode is 0, stated rather than defaulted. card.CardXrefRepository returns a discriminated outcome carrying a common.FileStatus value together with the CICS RESP and RESP2 and never abends on the caller's behalf, which is what gate G47 asks of it and what keeps the operator's screen intact; turning this arm into an exception or a non-zero exit would be the single likeliest way to diverge here. Gate G35 is consequently NOT asserted, and neither is G32, since the program contains no GO TO at all, nor G39, since nothing here paginates, nor G43, since this program has no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC, nor G40, since no XCTL is reached and no nextProgram other than this program's own re-entry target is named. WHAT IS ASSERTED: arm one of VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS runs to :208 - the account field is present and numeric, FUNCTION NUMVAL at :204 succeeds, and :206-207 store the value through WS-ACCT-ID-N, which is PIC 9(11) at :55, so ACTIDIN is renormalised to eleven zero-padded digits and comes back as 00000000050. CARDNIN is asserted UNCHANGED at the concrete value 9999999999999999 that the request supplied, and that value is deliberately not the one the cross-reference holds: the seeded row for account 00000000050 carries card 0500024453765740, so had :209 executed, CARDNINO would read 0500024453765740 instead. It cannot have executed, because SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN at :516-534 ends with EXEC CICS RETURN and is terminal - the task ends inside the arm, :209 is never reached and VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS at :235-249 never runs, which is also why every data field comes back blank, there is no confirm prompt, and there is exactly one send. The cursor is ACTIDINL, from MOVE -1 at :602; it is recorded as cursorField because a symbolic-map length item - the one whose name ends in L - is validation metadata and never a payload member. The six header fields come from POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :552-571 with the clock pinned to the same instant every case in this folder pins, practice B7: TRNNAMEO 'CT02' from WS-TRANID, PGMNAMEO 'COTRN02C' from WS-PGMNAME, the two titles byte-exact from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, CURDATEO as MM/DD/YY and CURTIMEO as HH:MM:SS. All 22 fields of the 218-byte communication area are pinned, because the conversation state travels in the payload rather than in any server-side session - rule R6, gates G37 and G38, the latter satisfied by the REENTER context with the error flag raised and the cursor set, on a screen that highlights in neither state. expectedWrites is empty and asserts positively that nothing was written, and TRANSACT's final state is pinned exactly as seeded. THE SEED: CCXREF is seeded ONCE, from fixtures/cardxref.txt, and there is deliberately NO separate CXACAIX input with rows of its own. app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines CXACAIX as DSNAME ...CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX.PATH, described there as the alternate index to CCXREF via the account key, so it is a PATH over the CCXREF base and the account-keyed read is an alternate-index finder keyed on XREF-ACCT-ID, never a second table - gate G45. The rows are seeded RAW at the 36 bytes the fixture supplies, not pre-padded: app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) plus XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) plus XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) plus FILLER X(14), which is 50, and the fixture omits the trailing FILLER. parity/FieldDiffer is the declared sole owner of that 36-to-50 pad and this case names the normalisation rather than performing it - gate G16, risk R-F. Every dataset is addressed by its binding key, and no fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears anywhere in this file - the dotted names live only in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD and in configuration, gate G46 - and no tenth fixture is introduced, the count being fixed at nine. The unit is invoked as a CONTROLLER_POJO: transaction.TransactionViewController is constructed and called directly, with no MockMvc, no HTTP and no JobLauncher in the path, so the arm is reached where its logic lives - gate G51. The 58-byte CDEMO-CT02-INFO extension at :72-80 stays a separate field and is never folded into the 160-byte NavigationContext, which is what makes the passed area 218 bytes. ACCTDAT IS A DEAD DECLARATION AND STAYS ONE, PRACTICE B5: WS-ACCTDAT-FILE at :40 appears in no DATASET operand anywhere in the program and COPY CVACT01Y at :89 is a dead include, so no ACCTDAT input is seeded here and no ACCTDAT row is expected in any channel of any case in this folder. The arm itself is likewise preserved exactly as written rather than tidied: the DISPLAY comes first and is not suppressed as noise, the message text keeps 'Acct' and 'XREF AIX file' verbatim together with its trailing ellipsis - it is a different string from the card-path text at :633 and from the browse text at :664 and :693, and the three must not be crossed - and the -1 goes to ACTIDINL and to nothing else. GOVERNING PRACTICES: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided', and that line is the whole document, so NO user rule governs this file; their absence is not licence to lower the bar, and the enterprise practices of Agent Action Plan section 0.10.2 bind instead. Cited by name and never reproduced: B1 no placeholders, so the DISPLAY rendering is derived rather than approximated and the injected pair is stated rather than left null; B3 the reference trees are read-only and not one byte of app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/csd or app/data was touched; B4, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12 as applied above; together with rules R1, R5, R6 and R7 - the EVALUATE keeps the source's order with WHEN OTHER last and reachable only when neither named response matches, which is gate G30, and the translation uses no GO TO. Gates G15 and G18 are served by this file simply being case10 of twenty and by its diff count having to be zero.
